papers.title: Statistical Optical Replication and Mixing of Spatial Information across Wavelengths
papers.abstract: Accessing and combining the spatial information carried by light at different wavelengths is important for linking structured-light encoding with spectrally distinct detection channels. Here, we introduce a correlation-enabled linear-optical framework for cross-wavelength imaging, bidirectional replication, and spatial information mixing. Shared random holographic modulation establishes correlations between nondegenerate optical fields, allowing spatial information to be retrieved from joint intensity fluctuations. In the demonstrated replicator, a spatial pattern encoded at one wavelength is read out in the detection coordinates of another through intensity correlations. Selecting diffraction-order pairs produces correlation kernels containing either the product or the conjugate product of two input field envelopes. These operations reproduce the spatial algebra underlying sum- and difference-frequency generation, while the optical fields retain their original carrier frequencies. The theory accounts for wavelength-dependent propagation and coordinate scaling, linking the input structures to observable correlation patterns. Together, these results establish a common framework for cross-wavelength spatial information processing through engineered optical correlations and joint detection.

papers.title: Particle dynamics in a microfluidic T-junction vortex flow: the role of history force
papers.abstract: The motion of inertial particles suspended in a carrier fluid, together with the dynamics of the underlying vortical structures, is investigated in a square microfluidic T-junction. The coherent structures forming near the branching strongly affect the particle distribution and may promote particle trapping around the T-region. Single-phase numerical simulations of the unperturbed base flow are combined with integration of the particle force balance equation, which, unlike most previous studies, includes the Basset-Boussinesq (BB) history force. The flow topology is analysed for $Re=500$ and $570$, while particle properties are varied through the Stokes number $St$ and the particle-to-fluid density ratio $ρ$. At $Re=500$ the base flow exhibits a steady vortex pair, whereas at $Re=570$ a Hopf bifurcation gives rise to a helical oscillation of the primary vortex pair characterized by periodic breathing. The BB history force has a non-negligible impact over the whole range of $(ρ, St)$ pairs investigated. It acts as an additional viscous force which, together with the drag of the relative motion, opposes the pressure-gradient force, widening particle spiral trajectories radially and elongating them axially. Its inclusion reduces the basin of attraction, indicating that memory effects promote particle displacement away from the vortex core and weaken trapping. At $Re=570$, spectral proper orthogonal decomposition characterizes the breathing of the primary vortex pair. Particles injected at a given location interact with the vortical structure at different phases of the cycle depending on the injection time, producing substantially different trajectories. This phase dependence is reflected in the shape and extent of the basin of attraction, quantified through the trapping probability over the inlet section and the probability density functions of the force components.

papers.title: PhySeqNet: physics-informed fluorescent foci detection for BARseq spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: BARseq enables spatially resolved gene-expression profiling across intact tissue, but its sensitivity depends on accurate detection and decoding of dense fluorescent rolonies. Existing spot-calling approaches can be conservative where signals overlap, while supervised deep learning is limited by the lack of reliable manual ground truth in real tissue images. Here we present PhySeqNet, a physics-informed deep learning framework for annotation-free fluorescent foci detection in BARseq. PhySeqNet trains U-Net detectors entirely on semi-synthetic images generated from an instrument-matched optical model combined with real sample-free experimental noise, and is integrated into pyBARseq, a modular Python pipeline for BARseq analysis. PhySeqNet achieved high detection performance on held-out simulated data across wavelength bands. On real tissue images, where ground truth is unavailable, we evaluated detections by forward-model reconstruction: PhySeqNet with conservative barcode-aware non-maxima suppression (NMSB) achieved higher reconstruction fidelity (NCC and MS-SSIM) than the BarDensr single-shot estimator, tuned classical spot detectors, and a pretrained deep-learning detector. In the analyzed brain section, PhySeqNet with NMSB yielded a median of 51 counts per cell versus 47 for BarDensr, with a similar number of genes detected per cell. The recovered transcripts produced spatial expression patterns qualitatively consistent with Allen MERFISH reference data and preserved cell-type composition after scANVI label transfer. These results show that physics-informed simulation can train practical, annotation-free detectors that improve BARseq sensitivity without disrupting downstream biological interpretation.

papers.title: Shear-driven arrest of dip-coating film entrainment
papers.abstract: A plate withdrawn from a bath of partially wetting liquid entrains a film above a critical velocity. Here, we show that this critical threshold can be substantially increased by the presence of a laminar gas flow opposed to the plate velocity that exerts a tangential shear stress on the liquid-gas interface. Using two-phase immiscible Navier-Stokes simulations and confining the gas to a narrow channel, we derive a closed-form expression for the interfacial stress, which combined with lubrication theory relates the thickness of the film and the contact line velocity to the applied shear stress. As the gas velocity is increased, the film thins and the contact line velocity slows down, until the imposed shear overcomes the drag of the moving plate and entrainment is arrested. As in the quiescent case, the velocity mismatch between plate and contact line is independent of the plate velocity and is set by the applied shear alone. We find that one set of varying gas flow simulations, with constant critical plate velocity, therefore determines the critical gas flow for every smaller plate velocity.

papers.title: Chiroptical Nonlinearity Found in Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Chiroptical nonlinearity is vital for modern optics and photonics. However, it remains a central challenge to obtain a material simultaneously with large second-order nonlinearity and strong nonlinear optical chirality. Here we uncover the strong chiroptical nonlinearity in COF-330-a, owing to the formation of unique chiral, polar structure with large p-electron conjugation via structural transformation. A large effective second-order nonlinear susceptibility of ~ 101 pm/V and a strong nonlinear chiroptical response (SHG-CD: -1.60 to +1.66) have been demonstrated in individual COF-330-a microcrystals, transcending the performance trade-off limitation in conventional chiroptical materials. These findings open a new avenue for designing nonlinear chiroptical crystals which harness the duality of polarity and chirality and chemical versatility of COFs.

papers.title: Judd-Ofelt analysis and coherent spectroscopy of europium-based molecular complexes for quantum information applications
papers.abstract: Rare-earth-ion based molecular crystals are emerging as a promising platform for quantum information applications, combining long optical coherence times with the chemical tunability of coordination chemistry. Here we present a comprehensive optical characterisation of twelve Eu$^{3+}$-based molecular complexes, with a focus on the coherent $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition at $\sim$580 nm. Judd-Ofelt analyses are performed across all complexes, providing insights into ligand-field environments, local point-group symmetries, and the resulting branching ratios of the coherent transition. We find that lower point-group symmetry (C$_1$, C$_2$) yields higher branching ratios of the $^{5}\text{D}_{0} \longrightarrow \ ^{7}\text{F}_{0}$ transition, exceeding 1\% in several complexes. Optical inhomogeneous linewidths measured at 4.2 K reveal narrow linewidths for some complexes of below ten GHz, indicative of a highly ordered crystalline environment. Optical coherence measurements of one of the complexes, 5-Eu, yields an optical coherence time of $T_{\text{2}}^{\text{opt}} = 2.3~μ\mathrm{s}$ at 4.2 K, comparable to the best-performing molecular systems reported to date. Systematic characterisation and quantitative comparison will be key to find structure-property relations guiding rational design of optimised complexes for quantum information applications.

papers.title: Predicting the Final Stationary State of Sheared 2D Euler Fluids
papers.abstract: The Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instability is a fundamental signature of the natural world, manifesting in phenomena ranging from atmospheric clouds to the iconic turbulence of Jupiter's Great Red Spot. While the linear dynamics of this instability is well-understood, the ultimate fate of the fluid --- the final stationary state to which it relaxes --- remains a formidable challenge. In this paper, we present a general non-equilibrium statistical mechanics framework that allows us to predict the asymptotic vorticity distribution of a sheared 2D Euler fluid. By constructing a self-consistent ansatz for the solution of the Vlasov equation, we determine the stationary stream function without explicitly solving the time-dependent Euler equations. We demonstrate that the relaxation leads to a population-inverted core, where high-energy states are fully occupied, surrounded by a tenuous halo of vortices in the lower-energy regions of configuration space. This result establishes the core-halo structure as a robust statistical consequence of the system's evolution, offering a universal framework for understanding the saturation of shear-induced turbulence in inviscid 2D fluids.

papers.title: Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals
papers.abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-André model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-André transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-André transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.

papers.title: Re-emergence of fingering in solidifying liquid-metal drops
papers.abstract: Solidification is expected to suppress fingering by removing mobile liquid. Here we report an unexpected re-emergence of fingering in impacting molten-tin drops: cooling first weakens peripheral fingers, but stronger undercooling restores them. At weak undercooling, fingers originate from a decelerating liquid rim and solidification reduces the effective acceleration that drives Rayleigh--Taylor-like amplification. At strong undercooling, solidification structures develop while liquid is still spreading, creating lateral mobility contrasts that redirect the residual flow. Comparison between the kinematically estimated solidification time and the experimentally measured fingering-onset and growth-termination times reveals a reversal in temporal ordering across the temperature range. A physics-based reduced-order model combines solidification-modified rim deceleration with mobility-gradient growth, captures the characteristic onset dynamics and accounts for the final finger length within the same physical framework.These findings establish solidification as an active means of regulating interfacial flow and morphology, with broad implications spanning metal-based additive manufacturing and debris mitigation in semiconducting industry.

papers.title: UV Fluorescence Sensing of Medical-Chemical-and- Biological Analytes by an AlGaN/Si-on-Sapphire Optoelectronic Chip
papers.abstract: This paper proposes and analyzes a compact fluorescence-photometer lab-on-a-chip that is simpler than a fluorescence spectrometer, and that does not require spectrum reconstruction by a computer. An on-chip AlGaN VCSEL lasing at 280 nm, or at 310 nm, pumps an on-chip sample in the form of liquid or solid or tissue, thereby exciting signature fluorescence in the 300 to 540 nm wavelength range. This emission signal is detected and read out by an on-chip UV-enhanced Silicon photodiode. The 2 cm x 5 cm chip consists of C-plane (0001) Sapphire, and no lenses, prisms, or mirrors are utilized in the photometer. The chip is opto-electronic and features co-packaged electronics using tiny electronic chiplets that are bonded to the sapphire. These consist of an LD driver and transimpedance amplifier for the UV photonics, together with ASICs, ADC, microcontroller, micro-battery and RF-wireless or Ethernet chiplets. The mission of this self-contained cost-effective chip is sensing targeted medical-chemical-biological (MCB) agents in a local or network setting. Eight significant MCB applications are detailed here.

papers.title: The binormal flow: a toy model for turbulence
papers.abstract: These notes summarize the content of a one-week course given by Luis Vega on the binormal flow model applied to describe the dynamics of three-dimensional vortex filaments in incompressible fluids following the Euler equations. This topic touches connections between the binormal flow, the Schrödinger map and the 1d cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, providing a rich casuistry linked to the physical and numerical phenomenology. This course was part of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ Advanced Summer School held at the Institut d'Etudes Scientifiques de Cargèse (IESC), at Cargèse (Corsica), from $20^{\text{th}}$ to $30^{\text{th}}$ June 2023. These notes have been written and completed by two of its attendees, Elena Danesi and Pablo Merino.

papers.title: Spectral-control-assisted Kerr-lens mode-locking in a Tm:Y2O3 ceramic laser
papers.abstract: We report a soft-aperture Kerr-lens mode-locked Tm:Y2O3 ceramic laser stabilized by suppressing wavelength competition under high population-inversion conditions. The laser delivers an average output power of 0.5 W with a pulse duration of 112 fs at a repetition rate of 90 MHz and a central wavelength of 2.08 um. Further optimization for shorter pulses yields a pulse duration of 107 fs, through with a reduced output power of 0.22 W. These results demonstrate that spectral-control is an effective approach for achieving stable mode-locking in such laser with strong spectral competition.

papers.title: Non intrusive parametric Reduced Order Models based on physics for incompressible flow
papers.abstract: Reduced order modeling provides an efficient alternative to high fidelity simulations for the rapid prediction of fluid flows in many query settings. Among non intrusive approaches, Operator Inference (OpInf) enables the identification of reduced dynamical operators directly from data while preserving a prescribed mathematical structure. The present work extends physics structured OpInf to the construction of parametric Reduced Order Models for transient incompressible flows governed by the Navier-Stokes equations. The velocity and pressure fields are represented using separate global reduced bases, and their reduced operators are identified directly from temporal and parametric POD coefficients. The identification procedure is formulated as a sequence of uncoupled least squares problems, leading to an efficient offline stage while avoiding the explicit projection of the governing equations. The approach is first evaluated on a lid driven cavity flow in a periodic regime to assess temporal extrapolation and prediction at previously unseen parameter values. Its applicability is then demonstrated for transient flow through a porous medium with a square obstacle, for which the nonlinear terms are not directly amenable to a standard Galerkin projection. The results demonstrate that the approach can accurately reproduce both velocity and pressure fields while providing computationally efficient predictions for unseen parameter values.

papers.title: Localization Landscapes based on the Green's Matrix of Non-Hermitian Optical Scattering Systems
papers.abstract: The Filoche--Mayboroda (FM) localization landscape predicts where the spatially localized modes of a self-adjoint elliptic operator reside without diagonalizing it, but the construction fails for the complex, non-normal Green's matrix G of an open scattering array of electric dipoles. We propose three real-valued, positive landscapes built from the Feinberg--Zee hermitization of G: a regularised Gramian inverse (Gram), the diagonal Schur block that carries the Metz--Neri--Rogers spectral density (SY), and the full hermitized inverse contracted against a polarization-isotropic source pair (Herm). The three form a progression from spectrum-blind to fully hermitisation-faithful, agree in the limit $z\to 0$, and diverge where it matters: at nonzero spectral shift SY resolves modes that Gram collapses, and Herm resolves modes that SY collapses. We demonstrate the progression on random and deterministic aperiodic scattering arrays with a wide range of structural correlations, extend to the vectorial case of transverse electric polarization (TE), and provide rigorous justifications along with mathematical proofs and a complete numerical recipe in the appendices and in the supplementary material.

papers.title: Bottom-Up Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for the Detection of Micro-Objects and Globular Analytes
papers.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. A correlative approach combining SERS, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy is employed to model the conditions required for sensitive SERS detection and spectral analysis of polystyrene microspheres (PMSs) as models of globular and vesicle-like objects. Based on these findings, we propose a SERS-active system that provides strong signal enhancement (up to four orders of magnitude for a single globular object) while maintaining spectral fidelity, where PMSs act both as model analytes and as integral components of a metal-dielectric resonator.

papers.title: Solitons in the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with the pseudo-Raman term, anti-diffusion gain and nonlinear loss
papers.abstract: We introduce a nonconservative nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) which includes additional nonlinear terms accounting for the pseudo-stimulated-Raman-scattering (pseudo-SRS) effect and cubic loss. An essentially novel feature of the model is the linear anti-diffusion gain, which leads to the obvious blow-up in the infinite or spatially periodic system. We consider the absorptive boundary conditions, which suppress the blow-up driven by effective convective instability in the setup. The NSLE model is derived, in the extended adiabatic approximation, from the underlying Zakharov system, which includes the viscosity term acting on its low-frequency component and the anti-diffusion gain in the high-frequency (HF) one. The latter term appears if the expansion, with respect to the deviation of the wavenumber, is performed not around the minimum-loss point (as in the usual situation), but around a maximum-loss point. Dynamics of moving solitons in the model is addressed by means of analytical and numerical methods. The sech approximation for the soliton predicts it as a stable fixed point (FP) of the system of balance equations for the HF norm and wave momentum, derived in the moving reference frame. The FP attraction basin is identified too. The predictions are corroborated by direct simulations of the full NSLE with the absorptive boundary conditions.

papers.title: All-optical deconvolution via quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy with bright twin beams
papers.abstract: The resolution of spectroscopic measurements is fundamentally limited by the convolution between a system's intrinsic response and the instrument response function, creating an ill-posed inverse problem. While entangled photons can theoretically bypass these limits, low photon flux has hindered their experimental realization. Here, we propose quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy (QCCS), utilizing macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler beams) to physically circumvent this convolution limit in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering. Employing the signal beam as a broadband probe, QCCS achieves all-optical deconvolution through a correlation-enhanced sum-frequency generation channel between the convoluted anti-Stokes and idler beams. By subtracting the uncorrelated background using a 500-femtosecond temporal window, we successfully retrieve narrow Raman bands (8 cm^{-1} and 15 cm^{-1}) completely obscured by a 75 cm^{-1} probe bandwidth without numerical deconvolution or prior knowledge. Our results establish macroscopic quantum correlations as a robust resource for high-fidelity spectroscopy, paving the way for ultrashort-pulse-free operando studies under natural, incoherent excitation conditions.

papers.title: Matrix-free numerical continuation of the Ikeda map in passive Kerr resonators
papers.abstract: We introduce a matrix-free numerical continuation framework for the Ikeda map of coherently driven passive Kerr resonators. The framework traces solution branches and evaluates their linear stability without explicitly assembling the full Jacobian matrices, using a unified formulation for states that recur after one or multiple round trips. We resolve stable and unstable branches of modulation-instability patterns and temporal cavity solitons, and uncover period-doubled homogeneous states and associated multi-round-trip dynamics that are absent from the standard Lugiato-Lefever equation (LLE). For period-1 states, the Ikeda map and the LLE show close agreement in the high-finesse regime, while their branch-existence intervals increasingly deviate as the finesse decreases. These results demonstrate that direct continuation of the unaveraged round-trip map can capture nonlinear states and multi-round-trip dynamics beyond the mean-field description, providing a systematic framework for bifurcation and stability analysis of Kerr resonators without relying on the averaged LLE.

papers.title: Silent breakdown of the perturbative polarization expansion in the terahertz regime
papers.abstract: Nonlinear optics expands the polarization in powers of the drive and retains only the lowest-order terms. This truncation is safe at optical frequencies, where the convergence field lies far above the damage threshold. In the terahertz regime, phonon polaritons enhance the nonlinear susceptibilities by orders of magnitude, lowering the convergence field into the sub-damage range and opening a window in which the expansion fails while the crystal remains recoverable. We term this window silent breakdown. At resonance, the nearest singularities of the driven lattice mode are a complex-conjugate pair of branch points below the multistability threshold, so the response remains smooth and single-valued even though the $χ^{\left( n \right)}$ description fails. The convergence field scales as $Q^{-3/2}$, so sharpening a resonance enhances the nonlinearity but narrows the range over which the expansion applies. It follows from the mode shift $S$ alone, $E_{\mathrm{conv}}=E_{\mathrm{ref}}(3\sqrt{3}QS)^{-1/2}$, giving 2$\sim$9 MV/cm for $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{3}$. Since resonant enhancement is central to terahertz nonlinear optics, this boundary defines the field range over which susceptibility-based descriptions are quantitatively reliable.

papers.title: Quantum Information-Theoretic Analysis of Optical Fiber Sensing via Stimulated Brillouin Scattering
papers.abstract: Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is a powerful mechanism for distributed sensing in optical fibers, as the Brillouin response is highly sensitive to local material parameters. Assuming the input probe is a quantum state, we develop a quantum-information-theoretic framework for SBS-based fiber sensing and intrusion detection. Starting from a linearized opto-acoustic Hamiltonian, we derive an effective input-output relation for a short fiber segment. We then model each fiber segment as a single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel and the entire fiber as a cascade of quantum channels. We then compute the quantum Fisher information for general SBS-dependent parameters and identify optimal measurement settings to achieve the quantum limit, comparing them with receiver-constrained strategies such as heterodyne detection and photon counting. In addition, we propose an adaptive approach that achieves first-order asymptotic optimality and provides a novel second-order correction to address preliminary miscalibration. As an application, we apply the framework to the fiber-tapping detection problem.

papers.title: Topologically steerable ultra-flat electro-optic combs via non-Hermitian frequency lattices
papers.abstract: Electro-optic (EO) frequency combs convert microwave signals to the optical domain with deterministic repetition rates, enabling applications in optical telecommunications, microwave photonics, and LiDAR. However, generating flat EO combs has remained a long-standing challenge due to exponential decay of the spectral envelope inherent to bidirectional frequency coupling within conventional schemes. Here we reveal the inherent correspondence between flat-comb generation and the topological energy bands of non-Hermitian nonreciprocal frequency lattices, and experimentally realize ultra-flat combs with topologically controlled spectral flow. We derive the exact analytical condition for flat-comb generation, and find that it maps precisely onto the complex energy band, thereby establishing a direct connection between comb-envelope engineering and non-Hermitian topology. Experimentally, we observe an ultra-flat comb whose frequency evolution direction is governed by the topological winding and remains robust against detuning and phase fluctuations. This scheme can be further extended to long-range coupling and multi-lattice architectures, underscoring its versatility for flat dual- and multi-comb generation. Our work establishes a topologically steerable approach for achieving ultra-flat EO combs, paving the way for chip-scale spectral engineering via non-Hermitian topology.

papers.title: Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor: Phase Contrast with Engineered Focal Plane Reference Speckles
papers.abstract: We introduce the Phantom Zernike Wavefront Sensor (phantom ZWFS), an engineered reference extension of phase-contrast wavefront sensing in which controlled pupil plane modulation generates off-axis coherent speckle structures that undergo localized focal plane phase shifts. These references may replace the central ZWFS reference when the on-axis PSF core is required for another optical function, such as photonic science coupling, or may augment a conventional central ZWFS response to provide additional wavefront information. Using a monochromatic scalar model, we derive the resulting carrier structure and show how the engineered references can be recovered through spatial demodulation and incorporated into calibrated reconstruction. A simple four-reference realization demonstrates that the reference geometry redistributes photon sensitivity across spatial frequency magnitude and orientation, producing mode dependent changes in linearity and cross-talk rather than a uniform improvement over a classical ZWFS. We then consider differential piston on a seven segment aperture as an application specific example. A hybrid sensor retaining the central ZWFS phase region and adding six engineered references that match the segment geometry gives similar precision near the phased state but substantially improved performance at larger piston excursions. Under the adopted photon-noise-limited benchmark, the hybrid reduces the nonlinear reconstruction error and provides better conditioned optical encoding of the piston state than an idealized vector ZWFS, allowing more precise piston estimation from the same detected photon flux at larger piston excursions.

papers.title: An anatomically grounded human-scale dynamic model of contraction-driven lymphatic pumping
papers.abstract: Lymphangions, the valved muscular segments of lymphatic vessels, pump lymph against an adverse pressure gradient. Current models resolve this pumping in one vessel, a short chain or a regional network, and whole-body human models are passive. We extend the passive whole-body network of a companion static study to the active regime on the same anatomical graph, with intrinsic contraction, dynamic valves and a respiration-gated venous outlet on every vessel. Without fitting the waveform or the contraction amplitude, the network settles into a bounded pumping cycle at the lymphovenous junction, at a clinical pressure of 7.5 to 12.3 mmHg and a drainage of 35 to 50 mm^3/s. Respiration adds a swing of 1 to 2.5 mmHg at the junction and contraction about 1 mmHg inside the duct. Pressure generation is limited more by load than by drive, and no single contraction amplitude fits every vessel. Raising the subclavian venous pressure from 3 to 15 mmHg lifts the deep cervical node from 8.6 to 21.1 mmHg at the weakest drive, a transmission of 1.04 that falls to 0.78 at the strongest, so contraction buffers cervical drainage against venous pressure. The same solver gives the human cervical outlet pressure that cerebrospinal-fluid drainage models prescribe.

papers.title: An anatomically grounded human-scale steady hydraulic model of the lymphatic network
papers.abstract: The lymphatic system returns 2 to 3 L of interstitial fluid per day to the venous circulation and drains the central nervous system. Most models of lymph transport describe one lymphangion or a short chain, so they cannot show how body-wide topology, calibre hierarchy and the venous outlet set pressure and flow. We build a passive steady hydraulic model on an anatomically derived graph of the human lymphatic system, with 1010 vertices and 1126 edges expanded to 89,060 sub-edges. Radii follow a Murray cube law, derived both from minimum work and from wall-shear-stress homeostasis. Pressure and flow follow from nodal hydraulic balance over Hagen-Poiseuille conductances, with an exponential wall law, hysteretic valves, Starling leak, node retention and a Windkessel outlet. Active contraction is off, and only the inflow scale is calibrated. Two quantities that are not fitted land in clinical range at the same operating point. Radii fall inside the vessel-class range, from 1.50 mm in the thoracic duct to 0.16 mm in the cervical collectors, and pressures stay below the 50 mmHg cuff scale on all sub-edges. About 49% of the gross load is removed before the outlet, nearly independent of the outflow scale and of the outlet parameters. On the route that drains the central nervous system, 30% of the superficial cervical load reaches the vein, at 10 to 18 mmHg along a segment that cervical-scale models replace with a prescribed outlet pressure. The model is a passive whole-body baseline for contraction-driven and clinical extensions.

papers.title: Conjugate heat transfer in turbulent pipe flow with azimuthally non-uniform heating
papers.abstract: Turbulent conjugate heat transfer (CHT) in pipes with azimuthally non-uniform heating is studied theoretically and numerically with a focus on low-$\mathrm{Pr}$ fluids. While the influence of the solid properties is well documented for uniform heat flux, their effect under azimuthally non-uniform heating has not been explored systematically. We address this gap by combining spectral analysis of the problem -- which reduces arbitrary boundary conditions to a discrete set of azimuthal wavenumbers -- with well-resolved numerical simulations of thermally and hydraulically fully developed turbulent pipe flow at $\mathrm{Re}_τ\approx 180$ for $\mathrm{Pr} = \{0.025, 0.71\}$, representative of liquid metals and air. Two principal results emerge: (i) the global Nusselt number is independent of the azimuthal heat-flux distribution and exhibits only a minor dependence on the solid properties, resolving an open question for low-Prandtl-number fluids; (ii) CHT nevertheless strongly affects the azimuthally resolved mean temperature at low $\mathrm{Pr}$, where azimuthal conduction in the solid homogenises the interface heat flux, and governs the level of temperature fluctuations through the effusivity ratio (thermal activity ratio) $K$. Finally, an analysis of the turbulent Prandtl number $\mathrm{Pr}_{t}$ shows a strong anisotropy, particularly near the wall, and a dependence on the azimuthal wavenumber.

papers.title: Deriving Schwarzschild and Kerr from the Einstein Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: This manuscript demonstrates that the Schwarzschild and Kerr metrics can be derived fundamentally from the Einstein Equivalence Principle (EEP) without explicit reliance on the Einstein field equations. We show that the EEP implies a gravitational stretching of length in the direction of acceleration, a spatial counterpart to time dilation. In the static case, this effect yields the constraint $g_{00}g_{11}=-1$, from which the Schwarzschild solution is recovered by taking the Newtonian limit. For the stationary case, we employ oblate spheroidal coordinates and construct a physically motivated tetrad to implement the EP, introducing gravity through three unknown functions. By applying the EEP-induced constraints and showing that the principle requires the preservation of the spacetime volume determinant ($g = g_0$), the system is reduced to a single unknown function that yields the Kerr metric. These results suggest that classical tests of General Relativity are, at their core, fundamental validations of the EEP. We further argue that the EEP leads naturally to Unimodular Gravity, implying that the existence of the cosmological constant is a direct consequence of this foundational postulate.

papers.title: Theory of Disorder-Induced Multimode Coupling in a Fabry-Pérot Cavity
papers.abstract: Strong light--matter interactions have attracted significant interest in physical chemistry due to the potential for modifying molecular processes by hybridizing with cavity photons and forming polaritonic states. However, for a disordered molecular ensemble within an optical cavity capable of supporting multiple photon modes, theoretical understanding of multimode polaritons remains incomplete, particularly regarding whether and how distinct photon modes are mutually coupled through molecules. In this work, we generalize the collective mode expansion formalism to incorporate multiple photonic modes and show that spatial and orientational disorder in the light--matter coupling strength (originating from dipole orientation fluctuations and photonic field inhomogeneity) can mediate cross-mode coupling. This disorder-induced coupling allows for energy transfer to otherwise unexcited photon modes through a mechanism termed disorder-induced multimode activation (DIMA). Using an effective one-dimensional Fabry--Pérot cavity as a test system, we demonstrate that the cross-mode energy transfer through DIMA can be controlled by changing the molecular layer thickness and the optical properties of the mirrors. Furthermore, we show that DIMA is robust against weak energetic disorder. This mechanistic understanding lays the foundation for a systematic control of multimode photon coupling using disorder-induced effects.

papers.title: Optimal linear-optical interferometers for unitary t-designs in a multi-photon Fock space
papers.abstract: We investigate the construction of unitary $t$-designs in a multi-photon Fock space on programmable linear-optical interferometers. Using the frame potential as the optimization objective, we identify architectures that realize approximate unitary 1- and 2-designs with considerably fewer controllable parameters than required for universal linear optics. For example, we find numerical evidence suggesting that for unitary 1-designs, the required number of programmable parameters scales empirically as $2d$ with the number of modes $d$, instead of $O(d^2)$. We benchmark the resulting ensembles using single-photon transition probabilities and average channel fidelities. Furthermore, as a practical result, we develop a photon-number estimation protocol for multi-photon Fock states that leverages these optimized 1- and 2-designs. Our findings demonstrate that shallow interferometers can accurately reproduce Haar-averaged first moments, while second-moment-sensitive observables provide a considerably stricter test for approximate unitary 2-designs.

papers.title: Early-time dynamics of the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability at Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic interfaces
papers.abstract: The Richtmyer-Meshkov instability (RMI) is initiated when a shock wave interacts with a perturbed interface between two materials, imparting an initial velocity to the interfacial perturbation. When the materials are viscoelastic, the subsequent evolution is influenced by the coupled effects of inertia, viscous dissipation, and elastic resistance. The interplay of these effects remains poorly understood and is important for predicting the dynamic response of shock-loaded soft materials, e.g., in blast-induced injury. Using the incompressible Cauchy momentum equation with a Kelvin-Voigt constitutive model, we conduct a linear stability analysis for the early-time post-shock evolution of a single-mode interface perturbation of two viscoelastic materials. We derive an implicit dispersion relation for the temporal growth rates of the perturbation. This relation depends on density, viscosity, and elasticity contrasts between the two materials and an viscoelastic parameter which is a bounded ratio of the viscous dissipation and elastic resistance response rates. Four material cases, spanning symmetric to highly contrasted interfaces, are examined to show how the viscoelastic number affects the growth rate structure as complex-dominated (oscillatory) or real-dominated (monotonic relaxation). The critical viscoelastic number separates these two regimes and is primarily governed by the density and viscosity contrasts. These results provide a theoretical criterion for predicting the early-time response of shock-driven interfaces involving fluids and viscoelastic solids.

papers.title: Coherent ultraviolet frequency combs generated by resonant dispersive waves
papers.abstract: Resonant dispersive wave (RDW) emission in gas-filled anti-resonant hollow-core fibers (AR-HCF) offers a wavelength-tunable route to ultraviolet (UV) and vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) frequency comb generation. RDW emission is expected to be coherent fundamentally, but various noise sources are expected to limit the coherence, including amplitude-to-phase fluctuations due to input pulse intensity noise and plasma formation. It is critical, therefore, to establish the limits of the coherence of UV RDW pulses to determine their applicability for precision spectroscopy. Here, we demonstrate the coherence of RDW emission at 260~nm generated with an amplified Yb-doped fiber system at a 2-MHz repetition rate with a self-heterodyne beat measurement between the RDW and the fourth harmonic of the source. We isolate the RDW contribution to the frequency noise by coherently subtracting the carrier-envelope offset noise contribution measured simultaneously with an f-2f interferometer. We observe a beatnote linewidth below 10~kHz over timescales longer than 100~ms, and we find a conservative upper bound of 1~rad on the integrated RMS phase deviations over a frequency range spanning 1 to 30~kHz. The dominant frequency noise contributions are consistent with environmental noise of the interferometers and AR-HCF coupling fluctuations. These results provide strong evidence that RDW emission is coherent under well-controlled experimental conditions, confirming its potential for UV and VUV frequency comb generation.

papers.title: Filter shaping in integrated photonics using non-adiabatic control
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that an array of integrated coupled waveguides can be designed to simultaneously perform the spectral filtering and routing of light. The framework that we present here operates in a regime opposite to the shortcut-to-adiabaticity techniques, but we show it nevertheless also only requires smooth, slow, and small, modulations of the array's parameters. Our design strategy rely on the analogy which exists between the temporal evolution of an Hamiltonian and the propagation of light in an array of coupled integrated waveguides, mimicking spatially in photonics phenomena analogue to the electronic transitions. Interestingly, the chromatic dispersion restores in photonics the correspondence between spatial propagation effect and wavelength dependence. Therefore our framework is able to fully reproduces temporal effects such as resonant transitions, making it suitable for filtering applications. As a design involving modulations, it shares similarities with Bragg-Gratings (BGs): but it adds some extra features that make it complementary in terms of applications and functionality. First it adds routing capability with the seamless management of multi-waveguide configuration. And secondly the framework we present requires only wavelength-scale modulations, order of magnitudes slower than for BGs. The effects we present here may not interfere with BGs geometry and functionality, and could even be combined with the latter.

papers.title: Unveiling Structured Optical Coherence in Nonlinear Optics
papers.abstract: Nonlinear optical interactions are typically driven by coherent sources. Recently, however, incoherent sources have also been shown to offer new opportunities in nonlinear optics. Here we study the effects of the source incoherence in second harmonic generation. We derive and experimentally validate an analytic expression for the far-field coherence function at the second harmonic frequency, which is a generalization of the well-known van Cittert-Zernike theorem. Unlike the linear optics case, here the results depend not only on the source spatial distribution, but also on the nonlinear structure of the crystal. We further show, by performing Young's double-slit measurement, that the coherence at the second harmonic increases as the light propagates inside the nonlinear crystal. Our results establish nonlinearity as a degree of freedom for optical coherence, opening a new research area at the interface of statistical optics and nonlinear optics.

papers.title: Engineering Nanophotonic Modes via the Radiation Continuum
papers.abstract: We demonstrate, experimentally and theoretically, a universal mechanism for combining nanophotonic modes relying on radiative-loss-mediated couplings. For the case of two modes this mechanism leads to a BIC-type phenomenon characterized by the emergence of a high-quality factor subradiant mode. This mode is experimentally observed in the mid-infrared range, in arrays of double-metal patch antennas where the radiation loss rates are controlled by the geometry of the system. As the mechanism described here is independent of the specific nature or number of the interacting modes, it can be used to combine physically different resonating structures, without requiring fine symmetry tuning or specific modal configurations, opening new opportunities for resonance-based nanophotonic devices.

papers.title: Exactly Solvable Diffraction-Grating Scattering Problems for TE and TM waves
papers.abstract: In J.~Phys.~A {\bf 31}, 3493 (1998), Berry provides an analytic solution of the problem of determining the diffracted beam intensities for atoms incident upon a grating given by the potential, $v(x,y):=iV_0(e^{i\mathfrak{K}\,y}-1)$ for $0\leq x\leq\ell$ and $v(x,y):=0$ otherwise, where $V_0, \mathfrak{K}$, and $\ell$ are positive real parameters. This result, which relies on the paraxial approximation, readily applies to the diffraction of transverse electric (TE) waves by the nonmagnetic optical grating given by the relative permittivity, $\hat\varepsilon(x,y):=1-v(x,y)/k^2$, where $k$ is the incident wavenumber. We show that Berry's grating belongs to a larger class of possibly magnetic diffraction gratings whose scattering problem for both TE and transverse magnetic (TM) waves are exactly solvable. Our analysis makes use of a recently developed dynamical formulation of stationary scattering that is based on the idea of mapping the scattering problem to the quantum dynamics generated by an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian operator. {We use this formulation to derive explicit analytic expressions for the diffracted beam amplitudes that are valid beyond paraxial approximation.} As a concrete example, we offer the exact solution of the scattering problem for TE and TM waves incident upon a generalization of Berry's grating.

papers.title: Transient Depth Thermography for Probing Heat Transport
papers.abstract: Directly probing heat propagation inside materials remains challenging because conventional measurements are predominantly sensitive to surface temperature. Depth thermography has enabled non-contact reconstruction of subsurface temperature profiles from spectrally resolved thermal radiation under steady-state conditions. Here, we extend this approach into the time domain, establishing transient depth thermography to resolve the evolution of internal temperature during heat transport. By exploiting wavelength-dependent optical penetration depth, time-resolved thermal-radiation spectra provide access to temperature as a function of both depth and time. Tracking this spatiotemporal temperature field enables direct probing of heat propagation and quantitative determination of out-of-plane thermal conductivity and interfacial thermal resistance. We demonstrate the approach in fused silica, obtaining thermal conductivity within 2% of established values, and measure the temperature-dependent thermal conductivity of MgF2 over a broad temperature range where existing data are sparse and inconsistent. Numerical simulations further demonstrate its extension to multilayer thin films for probing interfacial thermal resistance. By extending depth-resolved thermal spectroscopy from steady-state to transient heat transport, this work establishes a new optical route for non-contact characterization of thermal dynamics in bulk and layered materials.

papers.title: Towards stealthy hyperuniform networks with optimal isotropic complete photonic band gaps using a novel inverse design procedure
papers.abstract: We present a two-stage inverse design procedure for producing disordered stealthy hyperuniform trivalent photonic networks in two dimensions with isotropic complete photonic band gaps (PBGs) blocking light regardless of direction or polarization (TE or TM) over a wide frequency range. Most ordinary disordered systems fail to maintain complete PBGs as system size increases. The only known exceptions that remain open in the largest simulations have been generated by mapping stealthy hyperuniform point patterns into trivalent networks. However, the resulting networks are not truly stealthy hyperuniform two-phase media. Although their PBGs remain open, they are relatively narrow due to limited overlap between the TE and TM band gaps and broad band tails caused by localized defect states. By contrast, our two-stage inverse design aims to make the final network itself stealthy hyperuniform, achieving unprecedented near-optimal overlap between the TE and TM band gaps and a small defect state density at the band edges. We obtain not only single realizations with large PBGs, but a striking homogeneity across a large ensemble, effectively probing a network with 100,000 vertices. This ensemble-based band gap is comparable in width to the complete PBG of an anisotropic honeycomb photonic crystal with the same network parameters and nearly an order of magnitude wider than the previously widest known isotropic complete PBGs. Our designs can be fabricated using additive manufacturing, offering new pathways to manipulate electromagnetic waves for photonic technologies.

papers.title: Generating synthetic evolution of turbulent flames with an experimental data-based spatiotemporal diffusion model
papers.abstract: In this study, a conditional diffusion model -- a class of generative machine learning models -- is developed to generate synthetic, experimental data-based trajectories of turbulent flames. Generated experimental data corresponds to simultaneous field measurements, namely OH planar laser-induced fluorescence (OH-PLIF) fields and multi-component particle image velocimetry (PIV) fields, for attached and detached flame states in a swirl combustor configuration. This is done using an x-prediction flow matching framework combined with a pixel-based spatiotemporal transformer, which is capable of generating entire spatiotemporal slabs containing synthetic flame evolution at inference time, conditioned on the flame regime. Using this framework, synthetic flames were found to preserve key flame features and statistical consistency across space and time, particularly at the large scales -- deviations at high temporal frequencies and small spatial length scales were found to depend on the time-span of the generated space-time slabs. An extrapolation task of transition synthesis is also conducted, in which the conditional diffusion model is used to synthesize spatiotemporally coherent flame transitions (flame liftoff and reattachment) unseen by the model during training. This was accomplished using a model for the denoising transition velocity that relies on time-varying linear combinations of attached and detached denoising velocities, leading to an approach that (a) allows for control of the generated transition directions and timescales, and (b) retains sample-to-sample variability in the generated transitions in the process. Overall, this study provides a promising pathway for the utilization of experimental data-based generative models as a new means of data exploration in data-sparse environments, complementing both experiments and computational fluid dynamics-based approaches.

papers.title: Optically Incoherent Photonic Mutual Information
papers.abstract: While traditional evaluations of optical information transfer rely on disjointed abstractions to bridge electromagnetic propagation, coherence, and communication theory, we introduce an end-to-end framework that directly connects rigorous subwavelength wave physics to Shannon mutual information. By lifting the Maxwell current-to-field Green's function to propagate second-order field correlations (the mutual intensity), we establish a unified linear channel model that encapsulates coherent communication, phase retrieval, and incoherent imaging. Applying this framework, we demonstrate that the mutual-information-optimized photonic front end is dictated jointly by available spatial degrees of freedom, source statistics, and detection laws. For coherent sources measured by square-law detectors, we identify a structural transition: when detectors outnumber sources, topology-optimized front ends shift from point-focusing to interferometric mixing. This mixing leverages interference cross terms to make relative source phases information-bearing, yielding mutual information that surpasses the point-focusing amplitude-only baseline. Conversely, for spatially incoherent sources, the channel reduces to the Hadamard square of the Green's function. In this regime, under an isotropic source covariance, we prove that point-focusing uniquely maximizes the mutual information at fixed Frobenius norm. Under source correlations, the optimized front ends instead favor optical mixing. Finally, we derive closed-form upper bounds on achievable incoherent mutual information, governed entirely by the coherent singular values of the underlying electromagnetic operator. Potential applications include near-field microscopy, direct-detection optical datalinks, reference-free phase retrieval, fluorescence and thermal imaging, and structure-agnostic benchmarks for end-to-end-designed computational imagers.

papers.title: A robust and modular cesium magneto-optical trap using diverging laser beams
papers.abstract: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs) are a workhorse technology for neutral-atom quantum sensing, simulation, and computing. Here, we demonstrate a MOT optimized for inertial quantum sensing and precision metrology applications. Our MOT traps $4\times10^8$ cesium (Cs) atoms in a robust, modular system that achieves stable operation through two design features: (1) we use diverging cooling laser beams to reduce unwanted reflections and (2) optical elements are mounted in a fiber-coupled, compact, and modular cage rigidly attached to the vacuum chamber. Following polarization-gradient cooling (PGC), the system produces atom samples with temperatures below 10 $μ$K, similar to those achieved in conventional MOTs that use collimated laser beams. In addition, we observe trapping of $2\times10^7$ Cs atoms in a non-conventional MOT geometry, where the cooling laser beams are diagonal to the principal axis of the quadrupole magnetic field.

papers.title: A Unified Gradient Theory for Frame-Indifferent Rates of Tensorial Internal Variables
papers.abstract: We develop a thermodynamically consistent framework for weakly nonlocal continua with tensor-valued internal variables. Let $\boldsymbol{L}=\operatorname{grad}\boldsymbol{v}$, with stretching tensor $\boldsymbol{D}=\operatorname{sym}\boldsymbol{L}$ and spin tensor $\boldsymbol{W}=\operatorname{skw}\boldsymbol{L}$. We introduce the generators $\boldsymbolΓ_α=\boldsymbol{W}+α\boldsymbol{D}$, $α\in\{0,1\}$, which unify corotational and upper-convected transport. The resulting kinematic structure induces canonical frame-indifferent evolutions of both the internal variable and its spatial gradient, thereby providing a closure for gradient-dependent theories. Starting from the balances of linear momentum and microforces, together with an internal power expenditure depending on the internal variable and its gradient, we derive a local free-energy imbalance for incompressible isothermal processes. Under isotropy and inherited symmetry assumptions, this imbalance admits a canonical decomposition into contributions associated with $\boldsymbol{D}$, $\operatorname{grad}\boldsymbol{L}$, the generator-induced rate $\mathfrak{D}_α\boldsymbol{J}$, and its gradient $\mathfrak{D}^{\nabla}_α(\operatorname{grad}\boldsymbol{J})$. This decomposition yields explicit constitutive restrictions ensuring thermodynamic consistency and identifies the induced higher-order stress contributions arising from gradient dependence. Finally, we construct a coupled gradient theory combining viscoelasticity and constrained orientational order, in which distinct internal variables evolve under different transport mechanisms. The framework extends classical theories with tensorial internal variables, including Oldroyd-B and Landau-de Gennes-type models.

papers.title: Energetics and Stochastics of Extreme Waves Breaking over a Symmetrical Breakwater
papers.abstract: Rogue wave formation and enhancement over coastal areas have been documented over the last decade. This seems to contradict the observed low rogue wave (RW) probability near the surf zone. Without considering wave breaking, RW amplification is expected in this regime. To address this gap, we consider fully nonlinear effects of wave breaking through the proxy of height-to-depth ratio, spatial changes on the wavenumber through the WKB approximation, and slope-corrected refraction mild-slope equations on the energetics of irregular wave fields travelling over a breakwater. By increasing the significant wave height towards the breaking limit, the kinetic energy grows faster than the variance of the surface elevation due to nonlinearity. Thus, the kurtosis decays, albeit not to the point of getting sub-Gaussian statistics. We thereby resolve the apparent paradox of the occurrence probability of RW increase at the beginning of shoaling but subsequently decrease when wave breaking becomes dominant. Motivated by these theoretical developments, we experimentally probe inhomogeneous wave fields nearing the wave-breaking regime. We conduct unidirectional irregular wave experiments in a 30 m long wave flume, generating broad-banded waves over a symmetric submerged breakwater featuring a bottom slope of 1/5, allowing detailed characterization of spectral evolution and the persistence of elevated excess kurtosis even near the breaking limit for this steep slope. We thereby confirm that the excess kurtosis can still be large if the bottom slope is steep, and its maximum value is at least 4 times larger than in other ocean processes, occurring atop the breakwater and about half of its deep water peak wavelength distance after the shoal. As these conditions are typical near shorelines, this understanding is key to coastal areas.

papers.title: Mixing and sharpening at the interface of a two-layer fluid forced by random jets
papers.abstract: Understanding mixing at density interfaces is essential for predicting transport in stratified environmental flows. Laboratory studies have mostly relied on steady, spatially uniform forcing, whereas turbulence in nature is intermittent and heterogeneous. Here, we present experiments on a two-layer salt-stratified fluid forced by random turbulent bursts generated with a randomly actuated synthetic jet array (RASJA). Density fields are recorded with the light attenuation technique, allowing us to resolve the interface evolution. We measure that the upward velocity of the interface decreases with the density jump, in agreement with the power-law found in previous oscillating-grid studies. At large density differences, the interface sharpens during mixing, contrary to the smaller density jump case. Background potential energy analysis demonstrates irreversible mixing in both cases, with comparable energy changes. These results extend classical laboratory observations to a more isotropic forcing, offering new insights into the dynamics of mixing in geophysical settings.

papers.title: Phase Angle and Effective Second-Harmonic Generation Coefficient
papers.abstract: In this paper, the calculation formulae of phase angle are given for two classes of largest effective SHG coefficients in uniaxial crystals by means of the optimization theory. With the help of such calculation formulae, we present the best phase angles and azimuth angles of all uniaxial crystals class, as well as their effective SHG coefficients. Furthermore, these calculation is only dependent upon some principal subtensor of second order susceptibility tensor.

papers.title: End-to-End Quantum Key Distribution Across Hybrid Fiber and Free-Space Links with All-Optical Encoding Conversion
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) promises information-theoretically secure communication, but future networks must bridge fiber and free-space links that naturally employ different photonic encodings, namely time-bin in fiber and polarization in free space. Here we demonstrate a complete hybrid fiber and free-space QKD link that bridges both media within a single end-to-end protocol, converting between the two encodings entirely in the optical domain. Using the decoy-state BB84 protocol operating at 1550 nm, we demonstrate continuous secure-key generation over a 90 m outdoor free-space link. The system operates across atmospheric conditions spanning more than two orders of magnitude in the refractive-index structure parameter Cn^2, from strong daytime turbulence to quiescent nighttime conditions, and we further validate photon-level operation over a 750 m free-space extension. Throughout, the link maintains a session-mean quantum bit error rate (QBER) of 5.6-6.8%, well below the 11% BB84 security threshold. The encoding conversion is performed entirely in the optical domain without measurement or state reconstruction, preserving the security assumptions of the BB84 protocol. Consequently, the time-bin-to-polarization (T2P) and polarization-to-time-bin (P2T) converters remain part of the untrusted quantum channel rather than trusted intermediate nodes. These results establish secure photonic encoding conversion as a practical interface between fiber and free-space quantum communication platforms, providing a building block for future quantum networks applications.

papers.title: Symmetry-Informed Deep Learning for Electromagnetic Scattering
papers.abstract: Deep learning can accelerate the modeling of electromagnetic devices by replacing costly simulations with neural networks trained to map design parameters to scattering parameters. However, data efficiency remains a central bottleneck, as training data is typically generated through expensive numerical simulations. Here we show that symmetry provides a powerful and largely untapped route to overcoming this limitation in electromagnetic scattering problems. Leveraging the equivariance of Maxwell's equations, we obtain general transformation rules that map symmetries of electromagnetic devices to corresponding transformations of their scattering parameters. This enables both systematic data augmentation and the construction of exactly equivariant neural networks. We implement the framework for both discrete and continuous symmetry groups and demonstrate its effectiveness on photonic-crystal slabs and free-form diffraction gratings. Incorporating symmetry improves data efficiency by an order of magnitude compared to standard architectures, while equivariant models additionally enforce physical constraints exactly. Our approach is general and complementary to existing physics-informed strategies, provides a first-principles framework for constructing physically grounded surrogate models, and establishes symmetry as a unifying inductive bias for data-efficient and physically consistent learning in computational electromagnetics and beyond.

papers.title: Twist Engineering for Reconfigurable Optical and Optoelectronic Devices
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable optical and optoelectronic devices require compact tuning mechanisms capable of reshaping electronic, excitonic, polaritonic, and photonic responses without rebuilding the underlying nanostructure. Against this backdrop, twist has emerged as a powerful geometric degree of freedom that reconfigures interlayer coupling, momentum matching, symmetry, radiation channels, and chiral response by simply rotating adjacent two-dimensional layers or photonic lattices. In this Review, we survey twist-engineered optical and optoelectronic devices spanning van der Waals materials and photonic platforms. We first review the current landscape of twist-angle metrology, classifying existing characterization approaches into three complementary categories: direct structural imaging, methods based on moiré periodicity and morphological features, and techniques that infer the twist angle from spectroscopic or electronic responses. We then survey the principal technological routes for twist-angle control, including deterministic transfer and growth strategies, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-assisted manipulation, quantum twisting microscopy (QTM), microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), and emerging non-contact approaches, highlighting their respective capabilities, limitations, and prospects for programmable and scalable moiré photonic platforms. Finally, we discuss the future evolution of twist engineering from the fabrication of individual twisted structures toward dynamically reconfigurable, feedback-controlled, and manufacturable photonic systems. We further highlight MEMS-based rotation, piezoelectric actuation, and micro-LiDAR as representative enabling technologies and emerging applications within this broader landscape.

papers.title: Collective-State Preparation in a Subwavelength Triangular Trimer Using SUPER Excitation
papers.abstract: The Swing-UP of quantum EmitteR population (SUPER) scheme has recently been proposed as a deterministic method for the preparation of collective radiative states in two strongly dipole-coupled quantum emitters (Phys. Rev. Res. \textbf{8}, 013179 (2026)). Here, we apply this approach to an equilateral subwavelength triangular trimer of dipole-coupled two-level quantum emitters (QEs), loosely inspired by biological light-harvesting ring geometries, and demonstrate that tailored, time-overlapping, red-detuned ultrashort SUPER pulses can selectively prepare collective states in a $C_3$-symmetric system, including energetically degenerate eigenstates that are resolved through site-dependent optical phases. We find that both the state selectivity and the preparation efficiency depend strongly on the inter-emitter spacing. In particular, at deep-subwavelength separations, the symmetric collective state can be deterministically prepared with near-unity efficiency (approximately $94\%$), whereas the inversion efficiency and state selectivity are significantly lower at larger inter-emitter separations. Furthermore, this state preparation technique inherits a certain degree of robustness against reasonable static position imperfections and on-site frequency inhomogeneities of the individual QEs. Our results demonstrate that deep-subwavelength triangular trimers and, more broadly, highly compact ring geometries are excellent candidates for the deterministic preparation of collective radiative states via SUPER excitation. These predictions could be realized with solid-state emitters and molecules. Our findings offer a route toward the direct probing of the `pure' electromagnetic layer of interaction in biological and bio-inspired synthetic nanophotonic ring configurations, with possible relevance in photonics, quantum information processing, and metrology.

papers.title: Quantum metrology with undetected mid-infrared photons for applied non-destructive testing
papers.abstract: Metrology with undetected photons is an emerging technique that leverages quantum effects and photon correlations (entanglement) to retrieve valuable information in a target spectral range (e.g., mid-infrared, mid-IR) using measurements in an easily accessible domain (e.g., visible, near-IR). The underlying quantum process of spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is utilized to generate non-degenerate correlated signal and idler photons to serve as detection and probing photons, respectively. Sensing with undetected photons enables important advantages, such as ultra-low probe powers, room-temperature operation, and shot-noise-limited detection. In this contribution, we apply a quantum nonlinear interferometer based on an SPDC source to perform applied mid-IR spectroscopy, mid-IR microscopy, and mid-IR optical coherence tomography (OCT) as among the most promising techniques for quantum-based routine non-destructive testing. Moreover, we characterize the system, benchmark it against classical systems, and provide a prospective outlook for this new technology.

papers.title: Nanoparticle Arrays for Efficient Organic Light-Emitting Diode Emission Management
papers.abstract: OLEDs are increasingly applied in illumination and displays because they offer excellent color quality, are mechanically flexible, and are self-emissive. However, their usage is limited by low external quantum efficiency (EQE) and efficiency roll-off at high driving voltages. These limitations, together with demands for smaller pixels and device sizes in emerging technologies, motivate innovations that increase efficiency and allow replacing external optical elements with embedded solutions. Here, we demonstrate enhanced outcoupling as well as directional and polarization control of OLED emission, based on collective surface lattice resonances of plasmonic nanoparticle arrays that are embedded in the active layers of four different state-of-the-art OLED structures. Both square arrays and more complex lattices producing flat bands are demonstrated to guide the light to directions and polarizations determined by their optical modes. We show that by the design of the array geometry and the OLED structure, spectral and angular enhancement of the electroluminescence (EL), up to 30 %, can be achieved. Our results verify that surface lattice resonances of nanoparticle arrays offer a robust and versatile embedded solution for tailoring the OLED emission, as well as exciting prospects for efficiency increase if combined with narrow-spectrum emitters.

papers.title: Gradient-free learning of a closed-loop wall controller for turbulent drag reduction
papers.abstract: Closed-loop wall controllers learnt by multi-agent reinforcement learning are usually trained on periodic boxes far smaller than the flows they are meant to drive, and a large part of their drag reduction is lost when they are carried across. Retraining on the target domain is not an affordable remedy: the centralised critic that assigns credit to each wall patch degrades as patches are added, the zero-net-mass constraint couples the patches it is asked to separate, and the episodes must be collected in sequence at a cost that grows with the domain. We propose instead a short gradient-free refinement stage, applied to the transferred policy on the domain it will drive. An evolution strategy scores whole flow episodes against a regularised objective, so no credit has to be assigned to individual patches, and the candidates in a generation are independent and run in parallel. Applied to a recurrent multi-agent policy trained on a minimal flow unit at $\Retau\simeq180$ and evaluated on a channel sixteen times larger in wall-parallel area, a few generations raise the drag reduction from $19.0\%$ to $25.7\%$, above the $22.5\%$ of opposition control. Because the policies before and after refinement share an architecture and a training history, the difference between the controlled flows follows from the refinement alone. It shows in the friction decomposition, in the Reynolds stresses and in the near-wall spectra, and the actuation moves from a weak coupling to the wall-normal velocity towards a strong coupling to the streamwise fluctuation.

papers.title: Constructing mode-resolved quantum optical models for emitters in photonic crystals
papers.abstract: Recent advances are enabling quantum emitters to interact with photonic crystals, whose electromagnetic modes exhibit complex dispersion relations, spatial mode structure, and polarization textures. However, modeling light-matter behavior in these systems faces a persistent trade-off: electromagnetic approaches based on Maxwell-equation solvers provide realistic vectorial descriptions but are difficult to integrate with quantum many-body and non-perturbative methods, whereas simplified quantum-optical lattice models are tractable but typically rely on scalar and spatially independent light-matter couplings that miss essential features of these structured photonic environments. Here, we introduce a constructive framework to derive quantum-optical lattice descriptions that overcome this trade-off. Combining symmetry-constrained tight-binding constructions with numerically computed photonic band structures and field profiles, our method yields minimal, symmetry-enforced lattice Hamiltonians that reproduce the target photonic dispersion while retaining the mode-resolved (position- and polarization-dependent) structure of the light-matter coupling. We show that these models recover Green's-function-based emitter dynamics in the perturbative regime, while providing access to non-perturbative quantum dynamical simulations beyond emitter-only descriptions. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to a two-dimensional photonic crystal and show that it captures polarization-dependent directional emission inaccessible to scalar models, while enabling the analysis of non-Markovian light-matter dynamics and entanglement. Our results provide a practical bridge between classical electromagnetic simulation tools and quantum-optical many-body and non-Markovian modeling in photonic crystal settings.

papers.title: Aerosol generation by the splashing of low viscosity drops impacting liquid layers
papers.abstract: Using theory and numerical simulations, here we describe the early stages of the impact with a velocity $V$ of a drop of radius $R_d$ of a low viscosity liquid such as water against a layer of generic thickness $H$ of the same liquid. Our predictions for the initial velocity $V_t\gg V$ and the diameter $H_t\ll R_d$ of the toroidal rim bordering the edge of the thin lamella which is ejected radially outwards after the impact, are in fair agreement with both the numerical results and also with the experimental measurements reported by Zhang et al [J. Fluid Mech, 690, 5, 2012]. Consequently, the present findings can be employed, for instance, to predict the initial diameters and velocities of the fastest tiny droplets which are ejected right after a rain drop falls on a liquid pool, an ubiquitous phenomenon with implications in the dispersal of contaminants and in the generation of aerosols and of ice condensation nuclei

papers.title: Variable-Lattice-Density Optimization of Pin-Fin Heat Sinks under High-Reynolds-Number Flow Conditions
papers.abstract: This study extends variable-lattice-density optimization to high-Reynolds-number flows for the design of periodically arranged pin-fin heat sinks. Effective permeability and drag coefficient are identified from unit-cell Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes analyses of cylindrical pin-fin arrays and incorporated into a reduced model based on the Darcy--Forchheimer law for macroscopic design exploration. To enable stable optimization under high-Reynolds-number conditions, a dual-mesh framework is introduced, in which the flow field and sensitivities are evaluated on a fine mesh, whereas the design variables are updated on a coarse mesh corresponding to the unit-cell arrangement. For the base condition, the $L_2$ norm of the temperature deviation from the area-averaged temperature is decreased from 4.38 K to 1.00 K in the reduced model, and geometry-resolved analysis of the reconstructed design confirms a reduction from 5.98 K to 1.17 K. Additional calculations with higher inlet velocities and modified outlet locations show that the proposed method captures the dominant flow-redistribution trends under different operating and geometric conditions, although the thermal objective became less accurate when local solid-temperature variations became pronounced. These results indicate that the proposed approach is useful as practical design-exploration for identifying candidate pin-fin heat sink configurations under high-Reynolds-number conditions.

papers.title: Emergent coordination and propulsion of a model spherical ciliate
papers.abstract: A longstanding challenge in biofluid dynamics research is a mechanistic understanding of the coordinated movement of motile cilia and its resulting ability to facilitate fluid transport. In this study, we develop numerical techniques to simultaneously compute the emergent coordination of and propulsion by filamentous model cilia covering the surface of a sphere. To accomplish this, we develop what we refer to as the filament oscillator model, in which each cilium has two dynamic degrees of freedom: a phase variable that maps to a specific shape in a prescribed sequence, and an angle that describes the overall orientation of the sequence. By varying a parameter related to cilium stiffness, we show that there is bistability between symplectic-like and diaplectic metachronal waves, provided that the stiffness is sufficiently low. Above the critical stiffness, only diaplectic waves emerge. Further, we analyse the propulsive capabilities and flow fields of the two emergent states, showing that diaplectic waves provide more efficient propulsion due to their shorter wavelengths. In addition, we examine how introducing beat-plane tilt leads to ciliate rotation while maintaining nearly identical emergent states and comparable swimming speeds.

papers.title: Structured Optical Fields Reveal Nanoscale Chiral Light-Matter Interactions Governed by Optical Chirality
papers.abstract: Optical chirality has been proposed as the local electromagnetic quantity governing chiral light-matter interactions, yet in conventional circularly polarized fields its magnitude is locked to the electric energy density, obscuring its independent role. Here we create a structured optical field in which optical chirality arises spatially in magnitude and sign while the electric energy density remains nearly uniform. A single chiral nanoparticle exhibits a differential response that follows this spatial variation, whereas no modulation is observed for an achiral nanoparticle, providing direct experimental evidence that optical chirality governs nanoscale chiral light-matter interactions. Measurements of wavelength-dependent optical rotation further provide an experimental estimate of the chiral polarizability, predicting a chiral gradient force of approximately 100 fN and a one-dimensional trapping potential exceeding the thermal energy at room temperature under optimized aqueous trapping conditions.

papers.title: Quantized Photocurrents in Gapless Topological Matter
papers.abstract: The quantum Hall effect establishes that topology can fix a material response to integer multiples of fundamental constants when an energy gap isolates the relevant symmetry-protected electronic states. Whether such universal quantization can also emerge in gapless matter, where topological bands coexist with a continuum of metallic excitations, has remained a fundamental question in the field of quantum materials. Chiral topological semimetals provide a unique setting in which to explore this principle; when optical transitions are confined to a single chiral node, the resulting circular photogalvanic effect is predicted to be quantized by the topological charge of the node. In real materials, however, this nonlinear optical phenomenon has remained experimentally elusive, obscured by trivial band transitions, insufficient energy separation between node pairs, and their relative positions with respect to the Fermi level.
